output.headline: Court refuses bail to far-right activist Daniel Thomas over Channel dinghy
output.standfirst: Thomas, 37, faces a Portsmouth crown court hearing on 29 September after pleading not guilty to criminal damage; he was filmed apparently slashing a boat in the Channel while an emergency responder was onboard
output.bodyHtml:
Magistrates have refused bail to the far-right agitator Daniel Thomas, who was filmed apparently slashing a boat in the Channel with a blade while an emergency responder was onboard and has pleaded not guilty to causing criminal damage.

Thomas, 37, appeared at Basingstoke magistrates court on Friday morning, where he also pleaded not guilty to failing to disclose to police the pin number of his phone, under section 53 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000.

The prosecutor Kevin Lucie said Thomas was arrested at a BP service station and taken into custody, where police seized his mobile phone but he allegedly refused to provide the pin code.

Outlining the basis of the criminal damage charge, Lucie alleged Thomas slashed an adrift boat with a knife.

He told the court: ‘On 22 September, around 4.30pm, the defendant on his social platform livestreamed himself from a boat on the English Channel. He broadcast to a significant number of people a boat of migrants being supported by the RNLI in the English Channel. It was a single Rib [rigid inflatable boat] which was adrift.

‘He armed himself with a knife. He slashed the boat.’

Asked about the boat, Lucie confirmed he was unsure if the damage was worth more or less than £5,000, and said: ‘Unfortunately, it is the case that it did go back to France. We have asked for the cost of the damage.’

Thomas, also known as Danny Tommo, is a father of four described as a professional roofer. He was seen dabbing his eyes with a tissue at one point during the hearing.

He appeared for the hearing via video link, wearing a black top and grey coat, and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth. His teenage son and fellow far-right activist Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, also known as Tommy Robinson, supported him in court. Other supporters were placed in a separate room to watch a live stream from the court, a routine measure when interest in a case outstrips the space available in a courtroom.

Police kept a visible presence, with an officer in the public gallery of the courtroom, another at the courtroom door and a third in the seated waiting area outside the courtroom.

Dozens of police officers could be seen on Thursday evening monitoring several hundred people, many wearing black, who gathered outside a police investigation centre in Basingstoke, apparently in the belief Thomas was inside. The protest continued for several hours.

A hearing will take place in Portsmouth crown court on Tuesday 29 September, after Thomas said he would like a crown court trial. His lawyer, Simon Pentol KC, said: ‘This defendant is not charged with an offence of political activism, whether you agree with it or not, that is not the issue. He has elected crown court trial over criminal damage simplicita and nothing more, and for not acquiescing to a notice requiring him to provide a pin number.’

He added: ‘I invite this court to bear in mind it’s dealing with a 37-year-old man who lives with his long-standing partner and their four children, all aged between 18 and three, his partner is pregnant once again, four months. She is a full-time mother, he is the full-time provider, or breadwinner, as they used to say.

‘He is a professional roofer by trade. He is, therefore, having to look after his family who, through his political activism, have been under huge threat and due to publication of his mother’s home address, she has had to move home.’
output.progress: The prosecutor Kevin Lucie set out the criminal damage case in court, and a hearing will take place at Portsmouth crown court on 29 September.

context.text: The Crown Prosecution Service decided to prosecute Daniel Thomas following an investigation by Hampshire constabulary into an incident on Tuesday 22 September.
